summary: Add a --timeout flag to the existing CLI entry point so long-running commands can be capped. The flag accepts seconds, defaults to 0 (no timeout), and wraps the main command loop in a SIGALRM handler. Behavior is opt-in and additive — existing invocations are unchanged.
goal: Give users a way to cap CLI runtime without shell-level workarounds.

gotchas: SIGALRM is POSIX-only; platform guard needed for Windows.

behavioral_contract.title: Timeout flag caps runtime
behavioral_contract.description: Invoking the CLI with --timeout N terminates the process after N seconds with exit code 124.
behavioral_contract.evidence: Integration test wraps a sleep command and asserts exit 124 within N+1 seconds.

behavioral_contract.title: Default behavior unchanged
behavioral_contract.description: Without --timeout, the CLI runs to completion with no timeout wrapper installed.
behavioral_contract.evidence: Regression test runs existing commands with no flag and asserts behavior matches baseline.

phases.goal: Register the flag and wire the timeout wrapper.

tasks.description: Add --timeout <seconds> option to commander in src/cli.ts; parse as integer; validate non-negative.
Wrap the command dispatch in a SIGALRM handler when timeout > 0; platform-guard for Windows.
test_scenarios: Sleep command terminates with exit 124 when --timeout 2
Without --timeout, sleep command runs to completion

phases.manual_verification: Run the CLI with --timeout 5 on a long command and confirm it terminates.

success_criteria: CLI accepts --timeout flag without breaking existing invocations
Integration tests pass on macOS and Linux
